clue.text: A Dickensian double nominated in New South Wales package

parts.note: Sydney is the capital city of the Australian state of New South Wales
a carton is a cardboard package

explanation.surface: Someone nominated for a post in New South Wales is a lookalike out of Dickens, or perhaps a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Tale of Two Cities, the lawyer Carton looks so like Charles Darnay that he can take his place at the guillotine; his first name is the Australian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The character is famous as the physical twin of Darnay in A Tale of Two Cities, so he is that novel's double.

clue.text: Puts tension on snatches of music

definitions.meaning: stretches or tightens, as one pulls a rope taut

explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something tight is to stress it; separately, melodies heard in fragments are called by the same plural noun.

clue.text: Comparatively absurd dowry is forerunner of row

parts.note: dot is an old word, from French, for a bride's dowry
a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: A marriage portion that leads to a quarrel is all the sillier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel but means a line of seats; 'is forerunner of' just puts DOT before TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means slightly mad or silly, so the comparative form describes something more ridiculous.

clue.text: Alas! He doesn't cut out taxes in spite of his title!

definitions.text: Alas! He doesn't cut out taxes in spite of his title!

parts.words: Alas! He doesn't cut out taxes in spite of his title!
parts.note: the official's title reads as if he excises, that is cuts out, things, but his job was to collect duty on goods, not to remove taxes

explanation.surface: A lament that a tax officer named for cutting never actually abolishes any levies.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old British officer who collected excise duty on goods such as spirits and tobacco.

clue.text: Stored potatoes on the carpenter's bench

definitions.meaning: a mound of root crops heaped under straw and earth for winter storage
the screw device a woodworker fixes to the bench to grip work tight

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a farmer's earth-covered heap of root vegetables and the woodworker's gripping tool fixed to a workbench.

clue.text: Re unite separated suite

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are pulled apart and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A plea to bring a split hotel suite back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separated' rearranges the seven letters of RE UNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite can mean the group of attendants travelling with an important person, a synonym for an entourage.

clue.text: Alfresco opera in translation

indicators.note: translating moves a text into another form, so the seven letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An outdoor opera performed in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes 'in' as well as 'opera': OPERAIN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco is Italian for 'in the fresh', used of eating or performing outdoors.

clue.text: Leander's reception on the other side of the Hellespont

definitions.text: Leander's reception on the other side of the Hellespont

parts.words: Leander's reception on the other side of the Hellespont
parts.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the strait nightly to his lover, a priestess on the far shore, so his greeting there was hers

explanation.surface: How the mythical swimmer was greeted on reaching the far bank of the strait.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero was the priestess Leander swam to; the phrase also means a triumphant reception.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means an enthusiastic public reception, and here it is literally the greeting given by the lover named Hero.

clue.text: To go wrong with a twitch is irregular

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
a tic is an involuntary muscular twitch

explanation.surface: Making a mistake while twitching makes one unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic lacks a steady pattern, which is to be uneven or inconsistent.

clue.text: Are you, in an archaic way, not so much guileless?

parts.words: Are you, in an archaic way
parts.note: 'thou art' is the old form of 'you are'
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A question, in old-fashioned language, asking whether someone is rather less cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means innocent and without deceit, a synonym for naive.

clue.text: Proverbially, such creatures should be allowed to lie

definitions.text: Proverbially, such creatures should be allowed to lie

parts.words: Proverbially, such creatures should be allowed to lie
parts.note: points to the saying that warns against stirring up an old trouble by waking resting animals

explanation.surface: A reminder of the proverb about letting certain animals rest undisturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' reads as telling untruths, but the proverb means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'let them lie' advises leaving a settled problem alone rather than reviving it.

clue.text: Starts as I get among alternative spirits

indicators.note: the single letter goes in amid the other pieces, as a person mingles among a crowd

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
gins are spirits

explanation.surface: Beginnings, as someone takes their place among a choice of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get among' puts I between OR and GINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Starts here is a plural noun meaning beginnings or sources, the points things come from.

clue.text: Mrs. Swan's pseudonym

parts.note: a female swan has its own word, a writing tool's name, so the bird's name is a writer's assumed name

explanation.surface: The assumed name used by a woman called Swan.
explanation.walkthrough: A female swan is a pen; 'Mrs. Swan's' therefore gives 'pen' plus its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer's assumed literary name, such as George Eliot, is a pseudonym.

clue.text: Disconnect wires: it's more prudent

indicators.note: disconnecting breaks the order of the letters so they can be reconnected another way

explanation.surface: Advice that unplugging the cables is the safer course.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise means sensible, so the comparative means showing better judgement.

clue.text: Medico takes employment, part retrospective, with long running play

parts.note: MO is the Medical Officer, a doctor
use is employment, as in 'put to use'

indicators.note: looking back, so the word part is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A doctor takes a job in a long-running show, partly looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns PART into TRAP. Agatha Christie's play has run in London's West End since 1952.
explanation.definitionFit: Christie's thriller of this title is the longest-running stage play in the world.

clue.text: Una Morris disturbed by all-star Roman group

indicators.note: the letters of the name are upset and set out anew

explanation.surface: A woman called Una Morris is bothered by a star-studded group from Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Little Bear constellation is a group made entirely of stars and bears a Latin name.

clue.text: Garments for breathless people?

parts.note: someone out of breath gasps for a long time, so the clothing name reads as describing their panting

explanation.surface: Asking what clothes people who are out of breath might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is full-length trousers; read as a sentence it says such people pant long.
explanation.definitionFit: Full-length trousers, as opposed to the shorts once worn by schoolboys.

clue.text: Shell that's commonly cracked

parts.note: a hard shell around a kernel is broken open, and a person who is 'cracked' is mad

explanation.surface: A hard husk of the sort people often break open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' means broken open for the shell and crazy for the slang sense of a mad person.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the hard shell of a kernel; informally a crazy person, one who is cracked.

clue.text: Paint is upset by playful key controller

indicators.note: upsetting knocks the letters over so they land in another order

explanation.surface: Spilt paint is cleaned up by a mischievous figure in charge of the keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer at the piano plays and controls its keys.

clue.text: Youth takes two directions carrying a burden

parts.note: a lad is a young man
E is east, a compass direction
N is north, a second compass direction

explanation.surface: A young man taking two routes while bearing a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or weighed down with goods.

clue.text: Having an inclination to recording

definitions.meaning: leaning to one side, as a damaged ship does
entering items in a list or catalogue

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a ship tilting over and, separately, the act of itemising entries in a register.

clue.text: Spoken of as single combat fighter, he recognises contrasting ideas

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, so a similar-sounding word is meant

parts.note: a duellist fights one opponent in formal combat

explanation.surface: A duel fighter who sees both sides of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Duellist and the answer sound nearly the same; the answer believes reality has two opposed principles.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in dualism holds that two opposing principles, such as mind and matter, exist.

clue.text: The antithesis of a man's wife's scribed parents who are proscribed

definitions.text: The antithesis of a man's wife's scribed parents
definitions.meaning: a wife's parents are the in-laws, and the opposite of in is out
people banished and placed beyond legal protection

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is wordplay of a loose kind: swap the 'in' of in-laws for its opposite. 'scribed' is as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugitives declared beyond the law are the opposite, by wordplay, of a spouse's mother and father.

clue.text: Poetess Gertrude could have been a mug

definitions.meaning: the American writer and poet who lived in Paris

explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Stein was an American modernist writer, and the German word for a beer tankard is the same.

clue.text: Could a lost nest-egg be just this?

definitions.text: Could a lost nest-egg be just this?

parts.words: Could a lost nest-egg be just this?
parts.note: an egg laid in the wrong place by a hen, or savings put somewhere and forgotten

explanation.surface: Wondering whether vanished savings were simply put down somewhere and forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as MIS-LAID it describes an egg laid wrongly; whole, it means put somewhere and lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose something by putting it down and forgetting where is to misplace it.

clue.text: Investigate former African dictator with Oriental connection.

parts.note: ex means former
Idi Amin ruled Uganda in the 1970s
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Looking into a former Ugandan tyrant's eastern links.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect closely is to look into something, a synonym for investigate.

clue.text: Publicising the vocalist's denial when charged with playing.

definitions.text: the vocalist's denial when charged with playing
definitions.meaning: accused of playing an instrument, a singer replies '...'

explanation.definitionFit: To noise something abroad is to spread a report; and read as three words the letters give a singer's protest.

clue.text: Both sides of the political fence abandoned and in sound condition

definitions.text: Both sides of the political fence

parts.note: left means deserted or abandoned
right means healthy, as in 'right as rain'

explanation.surface: Politicians of every stripe, deserted yet in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: The two wings of politics are the socialist and conservative camps, the opposite ends of the spectrum.
